fatal_errors: The proposed HEBM-plus-SPS route does not reconstruct the target 6 GPa, 1473 K, 2-hour HPHT treatment.
The initial alloy and microstructure are changed from lamellar FCC/B2 Al0.7CoCrFeNi to unspecified single-phase FCC or BCC MPEAs.
The proposed clustering and dynamic-strain-aging mechanism is unsupported by cited evidence and does not address coherent FCC/B2 interfaces or interphase dislocation transfer.
The experiment cannot distinguish the target high-pressure effect from ordinary thermal treatment because it contains no pressure-matched or temperature-matched HPHT/HIP controls.
explanation: The response correctly addresses the broad strength–ductility trade-off and proposes measurable structural mediators, quantitative mechanical outcomes, and a falsification plan. However, it is not a reconstruction of the target strategy: the alloy, starting lamellar FCC/B2 structure, intervention, pressure–temperature–time window, hierarchical coherent-interface evolution, deformation mechanisms, and expected 1150 MPa/36% performance are all absent. Its alternative route is scientifically conceivable, but important claims are speculative. In particular, coherent nanoscale clusters do not automatically imply Orowan strengthening, dynamic strain aging is not established merely by a strain-hardening plateau, and mechanical alloying plus SPS can introduce porosity, contamination, and prior-particle boundaries that may reduce tensile ductility. The controls help test the alternative hypothesis but confound milling, consolidation, grain refinement, and clustering, and they do not test whether high pressure is the decisive variable.
